evidence.tokenizer_notes: All 4 models exceed 5% tokenizer discrepancy with o200k_base proxy -> CaseRow already carries both OpenRouter-reported and native counts (T-003 mitigation). Matrix report uses OpenRouter-reported as primary (billing-authoritative) with native counts logged for audit. Opus input_discrepancy 519% reflects Anthropic's provider-side expansion (tool schema + system headers injected before the model sees the tokens) — billing reality, not a defect.

evidence.decision_reason: Both variances = 10.0pp > 5pp threshold. Opus favors B by 1/10, GPT favors A by 1/10. Per-model registry used.
evidence.caveats: n=10 per (model,template) cell: a single flip moves variance by 10pp. The 'opus prefers B' and 'gpt prefers A' signal should be treated as weak — report methodology (VAL-401) should disclose this.

discoveries: Tokenizer discrepancies exceed 5% on ALL four models using o200k_base as proxy — contract's T-003 assumption (only some models need both fields) was conservative; in practice every CaseRow carries both. Fortunately CaseRow was already extended in VAL-101 to support this.

Opus input_discrepancy of 519% is explained by provider-side expansion (tool schema + system headers injected by Anthropic before the model sees the tokens). This is a billing reality, not a defect — matrix report cites OpenRouter-reported tokens as authoritative.
Both pilot variances landed exactly at 10.0pp (one flip in each direction, n=10). Small sample size means per-model preferences may not generalise; methodology should document this caveat.
No models were dropped — matrix is strong (4/4 passing smoke).
